  Investigating Compositional Challenges in Vision-Language Models for Visual
                                  Grounding

  *Yunan Zeng 1,2,3          Yan Huang 1,2 Jinjin Zhang 3 Zequn Jie 3 Zhenhua Chai 3 †Liang Wang 1,2
                    1
                        Center for Research on Intelligent Perception and Computing (CRIPAC)
                          2
                            Institute of Automation, Chinese Academy of Sciences (CASIA)

                                                         Meituan
                         yunan.zeng@cripac.ia.ac.cn            {yhuang, wangliang}@nlpr.ia.ac.cn

                            Abstract
   Pre-trained vision-language models (VLMs) have
achieved high performance on various downstream tasks,
which have been widely used for visual grounding tasks
in a weakly supervised manner. However, despite the per-
formance gains contributed by large vision and language
pre-training, we find that state-of-the-art VLMs struggle
with compositional reasoning on grounding tasks. To
demonstrate this, we propose Attribute, Relation, and Pri-
ority grounding (ARPGrounding) benchmark to test VLMs’
compositional reasoning ability on visual grounding tasks.
ARPGrounding contains 11,425 samples and evaluates the              Figure 1. Typical examples of testing compositional understand-
compositional understanding of VLMs in three dimensions:            ing of CLIP on visual grounding task. CLIP encounters challenges
1) attribute, denoting comprehension of objects’ properties;        in discerning the authentic object from deceptive ones. (Left)
2) relation, indicating an understanding of relation between        CLIP is misled by a dog of a distinct color. (Right) CLIP is misled
objects; 3) priority, reflecting an awareness of the part of        by an object within the phrase. Both instances suggest a deficiency
                                                                    in CLIP’s grasp of compositional structure.
speech associated with nouns. Using the ARPGrounding
benchmark, we evaluate several mainstream VLMs. We
empirically find that these models perform quite well
on conventional visual grounding datasets, achieving                21, 34, 41]. Many endeavors leverage the intrinsic visual-
performance comparable to or surpassing state-of-the-art            linguistic alignment representation within these models and
methods but showing strong deficiencies in compositional            integrate VLMs with explainability methods [37, 52] for
reasoning. Furthermore, we propose a composition-aware              image localization tasks. This approach serves to alleviate
fine-tuning pipeline, demonstrating the potential to lever-         the significant time and cost required for dense manual an-
age cost-effective image-text annotations for enhancing the         notation, particularly in tasks such as weakly supervised vi-
compositional understanding of VLMs in grounding tasks.             sual grounding [13, 20, 39, 40], weakly supervised segmen-

                                                                             As shown in Figure 2, ARPGrounding contains three
                                                                         types of compositionality: attributes, relations, and prior-
                                                                         ities. Each sample in ARPGrounding consists of an im-
                                                                         age containing two objects selected with bounding boxes.
                                                                         These paired objects serve as mutual compositional distrac-
                                                                         tors. Each sample includes distinct text corresponding to
                                                                         these two objects, and these texts can be differentiated based
                                                                         on attributes, relations, or priorities.
                                                                         Attribute. Our primary goal is to discern two objects within
                                                                         a single image. These objects belong to the same category
                                                                         but possess distinct attributes. Our objective is to assess
                                                                         the model’s ability to accurately identify the correct object
                                                                         based on the provided textual information. To locate such
                                                                         object pairs, we initiate the process by traversing the scene
                                                                         graph annotations of VG for a given image. We identify ob-
                                                                         jects with identical class labels, excluding those occupying
                                                                         less than 0.05% of the total image area, and then remove
                                                                         object pairs that overlap. This procedure results in two non-
                                                                         overlapping objects of the same class within the image, ap-
                                                                         propriately sized.

els in conventional visual grounding datasets as well, only
ALBEF slightly decreases in VG by 0.24%. Overall, AL-
BEF caft. becomes the best model, in comparison to all
other models, and in ARPGrounding-Priority, it lags be-
hind only METER. Figure 4 illustrates some visualization
results, more visualization results are shown in Appendix.
    In general, our proposed composition-aware fine-tuning
yields significant improvements in ARPGrounding and also
enhances performance in conventional visual grounding
datasets. Our results underscore the efficacy of extract-
ing rich information from diverse textual sources related to          Figure 4. Visualization of grounding results of ALBEF and AL-
an image, even in the absence of dense annotations, lead-             BEF caft. From left to right, the three columns depict the orig-
ing to substantial advancements in compositional under-               inal image, the heatmap generated by ALBEF, and the heatmap
standing. While diverse vision-language pre-training ob-              generated by ALBEF caft. We demonstrate that our composition-
jectives contribute significantly to representation learning,         aware fine-tuning pipeline effectively enhances compositional un-
Ma et al. [28] suggests that merely expanding the scale               derstanding.
of pre-training datasets is ineffective in capturing compo-
sitional structures. Hence, we furnish evidence support-
ing the notion that pursuing algorithmic enhancements can
augment model capacity through the utilization of cost-
effective image-text annotations.

                                                                                    6. Conclusion
                                                                                        In this paper, we first employ explainability techniques
of text that pertain to distinct objects. We design two text                        to achieve state-of-the-art results in weakly supervised vi-
pair variants including (1) text pair that refers to the same
                                                                                    sual grounding tasks using VLMs. We then introduce
object and (2) text pair that is randomly sampled. We fol-
                                                                                    ARPGrounding, a novel benchmark, and reveal the lim-
low the composition-aware fine-tuning pipeline but use dif-
                                                                                    itations of VLMs in fine-grained visio-linguistic compo-
ferent training data. Results of fine-tuning CLIP and AL-                           sitionality. To address these challenges, we propose a
BEF with these two variants are shown in Table 3. It can                            composition-aware fine-tuning pipeline that significantly
be observed that fine-tuning with text pair (1) adversely af-                       enhances VLMs’ compositional understanding without re-
fects grounding performance. Conversely, fine-tuning with
                                                                                    lying on dense annotations.
text pair (2) contributes to improved performance. This is                          Acknowledgment.             This work was jointly sup-
